what: Knight-Swift is the largest full-truckload carrier in the United States. It hauls freight by the trailer load, runs a less-than-truckload network, brokers freight it cannot carry, and leases trucks to owner-operators.
customers: Retailers, manufacturers and food companies shipping full trailers across the country.
money: dry van and refrigerated full-load freight
moat: Scale in a fragmented industry: tens of thousands of trucks mean density on lanes, better equipment costs and the ability to serve a national shipper that a small carrier cannot.
risks: Truckload rates have been depressed for three years by excess capacity
A 0.9% net margin: the freight recession has taken almost all the profit
67 times earnings on that depressed profit
opportunities: $753M of free cash flow despite the downturn, about 13 times cash flow
Analysts see about 38% upside, with 20 covering the stock
The LTL network bought from USA Truck and Dependable earns better margins than truckload and is growing
watch: Truckload spot rates and the LTL network's operating ratio.
